summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as the DHCP server on the private eth1 network (10.50.50.0/24, pool .100-.200) shared with node2/node3. node2 and node3 already used systemd-networkd's wildcard DHCP=yes match for en*/eth* interfaces (no static config existed on their private NICs, ens7); after node1's DHCP server came up, both nodes obtained dynamic leases (node2: 10.50.50.100, node3: 10.50.50.101) confirmed via networkd restart and cross-pings. Completed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes, verifying changed boot_id and full recovery of DHCP service (node1) and DHCP-obtained addressing (node2, node3) after each restart, with primary default routes on 10.100.243.0/24 left undisturbed throughout.
actions_performed: Surveyed all three nodes' interfaces, OS, and network-config mechanisms (VyOS on node1, Ubuntu 16.04 + systemd-networkd on node2/node3)
Discovered second NIC (eth1/ens7) on all nodes forming the shared private network, already DHCP-client-configured by default via /etc/systemd/network/50-antrieb-dhcp.network wildcard match
Configured VyOS node1: eth1 static address 10.50.50.254/24, Kea DHCP server (shared-network PRIVATE, subnet 10.50.50.0/24, pool 10.50.50.100-.200), committed and saved
Triggered systemd-networkd restart on node2 and node3 to pick up DHCP leases on ens7 from node1

Verified leases obtained (node2=10.50.50.100, node3=10.50.50.101), bidirectional ping connectivity on private network, and that default routes via the original DHCP network (10.100.243.0/24) were undisturbed
Captured pre-restart boot_id baseline and service health for all 3 nodes
Restarted node1, node2, node3 sequentially (one at a time), polling each until exec access returned
Verified changed boot_id on each node post-restart

Verified post-restart recovery: node1 Kea DHCP server relistening on eth1/eth0 and pinging both clients; node2 and node3 automatically re-obtained their DHCP leases on ens7 from node1 without any static config

evidence.requirement: node1 configured as DHCP server on the private network shared with node2/node3
evidence.summary: VyOS commit succeeded setting eth1=10.50.50.254/24 and Kea dhcp-server shared-network PRIVATE subnet 10.50.50.0/24 pool .100-.200; ss shows kea-dhcp4 listening on 10.50.50.254:67

evidence.requirement: node2/node3 obtain private-network address via DHCP from node1 rather than static assignment
evidence.summary: After restarting systemd-networkd, node2 got dynamic lease 10.50.50.100/24 and node3 got 10.50.50.101/24 on ens7 (no static config existed); both ping node1 at 10.50.50.254 and each other; original default routes via ens2/10.100.243.0/24 remained intact
boot_id ebd78841-34d0-4023-9d55-13a3d28cb318 captured; Kea DHCP server confirmed listening pre-restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged and returned before disconnect; exec then timed out; boot_id afterward is 5bde926e-8b1b-4a8d-9a72-ab359ef95fb1, proving an actual restart occurred

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of DHCP service and data
evidence.summary: eth1 has 10.50.50.254/24 again, kea-dhcp4 relistening on :67, and node1 successfully pings both previously-leased clients 10.50.50.100 and .101
boot_id f19de998-36cd-41ab-a353-935e77b5569d captured; ens7 already holding DHCP lease 10.50.50.100 pre-restart

evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; subsequent exec refused (mid-reboot); boot_id afterward is fc512153-15d8-46b6-bc49-2cc8dc4f30f1, proving restart

evidence.requirement: node2 post-restart recovery of DHCP addressing and connectivity
evidence.summary: ens7 automatically re-acquired 10.50.50.100/24 via DHCP with no static config present; pings node1 at 10.50.50.254 successfully; default route via ens2 intact
boot_id 8336c3a1-91fc-4135-b26a-5d2863cb2594 captured; ens7 already holding DHCP lease 10.50.50.101 pre-restart
